positions.name: GateMandateDeclaration
positions.frame: What counts as the settled specification of the deployment gate — the mandate, its scope, and its accountable owner — as distinct from the case made for it?
positions.why: src-1's opening declarative ('now requires a signed release manifest before it ships'), src-3's labeled Gate rule, src-4's Scope line, and src-5's Owner line all perform the same directional move: a settled, protocol-formal, authority-ranking act that ratifies the mandate rather than argues for it — the dimensional reads converge here (register: same ProtocolGateSpec mint across all four; relational: same GateOwnerDeclaresMandate mint across all four; conviction: all four sit at 'decision', i.e. enacted, not argued). src-2, by contrast, sits at 'claim' conviction, in market-pricing/informational register rather than authority-ranking, and is concrete-past rather than abstract-present — it defends the gate's existence rather than constituting it, so the conviction gradient argues against folding it into this set.
